KO.rationale: Coca-Cola is a world-class franchise with irreplicable brand equity ($46.3B), an asset-light concentrate model generating ~28% net margins, 40.4% ROE, and 62+ years of dividend increases. However, the stock is extremely expensive relative to its own history and current interest-rate environment, and the near-term catalyst picture is ambiguous-to-negative. P/E of 28.44x sits at the 96th percentile of its 365-day range (23.2–29.6x), representing ~5 turns of multiple expansion over the past year with no commensurate step-up in earnings quality — net margin held flat at 25.9% and ROE at 40.4%. The earnings yield of 3.5% now trades 90bps below the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.40%, a notable inversion for a defensive compounder. OCF was deeply negative at -$5.20B in Q1 2025, and with only two quarters of data available, cash generation durability is unverified. The IRS tax dispute ($20B case, potential ~$6B liability) is excluded from 2026 tax guidance and represents a binary downside risk. Berkshire Hathaway's portfolio rebalancing — Greg Abel elevating Alphabet above KO in the portfolio — is a mild sentiment headwind from the largest single holder. CSD structural decline (~69% of volume from carbonates) faces compounding headwinds from GLP-1 adoption, MAHA politics, and expanding sugar taxes (Mexico 2026 excise). While Zero Sugar's 14% growth and Q1 2026's 10% organic revenue growth are encouraging, the market has already priced this quality aggressively. Mean-reversion of P/E toward the 23–25x band implies 10–17% downside. The risk/reward is asymmetric to the downside at current levels.
